natural: the threshold wears through

meaning.en: So many visitors that the doorsill is worn through; a house always crowded with callers.
meaning.zh: 门槛都被踏穿了，形容来访的人极多。

examples.zh: 名医的诊所前求医者络绎不绝，户限为穿。
examples.en: Patients thronged the famous doctor's clinic until the threshold was worn through.

examples.zh: 他书法远近闻名，求字者户限为穿。
examples.en: His calligraphy is known far and wide and people seeking his writing wear out his doorstep.

usage.en: Praises popularity or fame; 限 is 'threshold'. Close to 踏破门槛.
usage.zh: 称赞声名显赫、来访者多；“限”指门槛；近“踏破门槛”。

literal: hold in bosom · fine jade · grasp · fine jade
natural: clasp precious jade in one's bosom and hand

meaning.en: To possess pure moral character and outstanding talent.
meaning.zh: 怀里握着美玉，比喻人品高洁、才能出众。

equivalents: pure of character and rich in talent

examples.zh: 他怀瑾握瑜，却甘于淡泊。
examples.en: He has pure virtue and rare talent, yet is content to be plain.

examples.zh: 这位学者怀瑾握瑜，深受学生敬重。
examples.en: The scholar is both talented and upright, and greatly respected by students.

story.en: In 'Embracing Sand', Qu Yuan laments: 'Holding fine jade in my bosom and hand, in my poverty there is none to whom to show it.'
story.zh: 屈原《九章·怀沙》：“怀瑾握瑜兮，穷不得所示。”

usage.en: Praise combining virtue and talent; sometimes used when such a person is overlooked. 瑾 and 瑜 are both fine jades.
usage.zh: 赞美德才兼备；有时暗含怀才不遇之意；“瑾”“瑜”皆美玉。

natural: carry talent, embrace ability

meaning.en: To possess talent and ability that are waiting for the right opportunity.
meaning.zh: 身怀才能，等待施展的机会。

examples.zh: 他怀才抱器，等待时机一展抱负。
examples.en: He has talent and ability and is waiting for the chance to realise his ambitions.

examples.zh: 怀才抱器之士，不该被埋没。
examples.en: Gifted people should not be left unused.

usage.en: Sympathetic; implies the talent is not yet recognised. Note 才 and 器 both mean ability.
usage.zh: 含同情，暗示才能未被重用；“才”“器”皆指才能。

natural: change the bones and steal the embryo

meaning.en: In writing, to build on an earlier work's ideas but remake it so that it feels new.
meaning.zh: 在文学创作中，借鉴前人诗文的意思而加以变化，翻出新意。

examples.zh: 这首词换骨夺胎，在旧意上翻出了新境界。
examples.en: This lyric recasts older ideas and opens a new realm.

examples.zh: 好的改编不能照抄，要换骨夺胎。
examples.en: A good adaptation should not copy but remake.

origin.source: 惠洪《冷斋夜话》引黄庭坚语

story.en: The monk Huihong records Huang Tingjian as saying that borrowing a poet's meaning with new words is 'changing the bones', and shaping the original idea afresh is 'taking the embryo'.
story.zh: 《冷斋夜话》引黄庭坚：“不易其意而造其语，谓之换骨法；规摹其意而形容之，谓之夺胎法。”

usage.en: A term from Song poetics; praises creative reworking. Not the same as 脱胎换骨, which means a total personal transformation.
usage.zh: 宋代诗论术语，赞赏创造性借鉴；与“脱胎换骨”（彻底改造）不同。

natural: put fire beneath piled firewood

meaning.en: To leave a hidden danger that may burst into flame at any moment; a false sense of safety.
meaning.zh: 把火放在堆积的柴草下，比喻潜伏着极大的危险。

examples.zh: 放任问题不管，无异于积薪厝火。
examples.en: Ignoring the problem is like laying a fire under stacked firewood.

examples.zh: 存着隐患却不处理，实乃积薪厝火。
examples.en: Keeping a known risk without dealing with it is sitting on a powder keg.

story.en: In his memorial on governing, Jia Yi warns that the present peace is like putting fire under piled firewood and sleeping on top, calling it ‘safe’.
story.zh: 《汉书·贾谊传》：“夫抱火厝之积薪之下而寝其上，火未及然，因谓之安。”

usage.en: A serious warning about latent risk; 厝 here reads cuò (to place).
usage.zh: 对潜在风险的严重警告；“厝”读 cuò，放置之意。

natural: every household supplied, every person content

meaning.en: A prosperous society where everyone has enough.
meaning.zh: 家家衣食丰足，人人生活富裕。

examples.zh: 丰年之后，家给人足，一派祥和。
examples.en: After a good harvest every family was well off and all was peaceful.

examples.zh: 为政者的目标是让百姓家给人足。
examples.en: The aim of those in government is that people have enough.

usage.en: Describes an ideal state of affairs; read 给 as jǐ (to supply).
usage.zh: 形容理想的富足景象；“给”读 jǐ，供给之意。

natural: Jie's dog barks at Yao

meaning.en: A dog serves its own master even if the stranger is a sage; people act loyally to their patron regardless of right and wrong.
meaning.zh: 桀的狗对着尧狂叫，比喻奴才一心效忠主子，不辨是非。

equivalents: a dog loyal to a bad master
blind loyalty to the wrong side

examples.zh: 他不过是桀犬吠尧，替老板攻击对手。
examples.en: He is merely barking at his boss's rivals out of blind loyalty.

examples.zh: 别把桀犬吠尧当成正义，盲从毫无意义。
examples.en: Don't mistake blind loyalty for justice; mindless obedience means nothing.

story.en: In Zou Yang's letter from prison, he notes that ‘Jie's dog can be made to bark at Yao’, since a dog bites those who are not its master's.
story.zh: 《史记·鲁仲连邹阳列传》载邹阳狱中上书：“桀之犬可使吠尧，跖之客可使刺由。”

usage.en: Derogatory about blind loyalty; the name Jie (tyrant) and Yao (sage) set the moral contrast.
usage.zh: 贬义，指盲目效忠；桀（暴君）与尧（圣君）形成对照。

natural: the nine cauldrons and the great bell

meaning.en: Extremely weighty and authoritative, whether a person's words or standing.
meaning.zh: 九鼎和大吕都是极贵重的重器，比喻分量极重、地位或言论极有权威。

examples.zh: 他一句话九鼎大吕，全场鸦雀无声。
examples.en: His single word carried great weight and the hall fell silent.

examples.zh: 这位前辈在业界地位九鼎大吕。
examples.en: This senior figure's standing in the industry is of the utmost weight.

story.en: Maoxu says that Master Mao by going to Chu made Zhao weightier than the nine cauldrons and the great bell.
story.zh: 《史记·平原君虞卿列传》：“毛先生一至楚，而使赵重于九鼎大吕。”

usage.en: Praises weight and authority; 吕 is lǚ. Often said as 重于九鼎大吕.
usage.zh: 形容分量或权威极大；“吕”读 lǚ；常说“重于九鼎大吕”。

natural: enough mosquitoes make a thunderclap

meaning.en: Many small voices together can create great noise; slander or rumour growing from small beginnings.
meaning.zh: 蚊子聚集，声音可如雷鸣，比喻谣言、坏话积少成多，影响很大。

examples.zh: 网络上聚蚊成雷，一条谣言毁了他的名声。
examples.en: Online, countless small voices make a roar and a single rumour ruined his reputation.

examples.zh: 别小看流言，聚蚊成雷的后果很严重。
examples.en: Don't underestimate gossip; when it piles up the consequences are serious.

story.en: In the biography of Prince Liu Jian, it is said that when many mouths blow they can move mountains, and a swarm of mosquitoes can make a thunder.
story.zh: 《汉书·景十三王传》：“夫众喣漂山，聚蚊成雷，朋党执虎，十人成市虎之化。”

usage.en: Warns about the power of accumulated gossip; also used of mounting public pressure.
usage.zh: 警示流言积累的力量，也可指群众舆论的压力。

literal: face up · countenance · act as · teacher
natural: hold up one's face and act as teacher

meaning.en: To take on the role of teacher with dignity, undeterred by criticism or mockery.
meaning.zh: 态度严正地以师自居，不惧别人议论。

equivalents: act as a teacher without flinching
take the role of master boldly

examples.zh: 他在世人讥笑中抗颜为师，坚持传道。
examples.en: Amid ridicule he boldly took up the teacher's role and kept on teaching.

examples.zh: 当年韩愈抗颜为师，为学者树立典范。
examples.en: Han Yu dared to teach as a master and set an example for scholars.

origin.source: 柳宗元《答韦中立论师道书》

story.en: Liu Zongyuan notes that Han Yu alone dared to defy common opinion and ridicule, gathering students and writing the ‘Discourse on Teachers’, thus ‘facing the world as a teacher’.
story.zh: 柳宗元《答韦中立论师道书》：“独韩愈奋不顾流俗，犯笑侮，收召后学，作《师说》，因抗颜而为师。”

usage.en: Originally praised courage in teaching; may also describe someone who poses as a teacher. 颜 means 'face'.
usage.zh: 原赞不畏流俗而教人，也可指自居师长；“颜”指面孔。

natural: bareheaded and barefoot

meaning.en: Bareheaded and barefoot; an unrestrained, informal or plain way of living.
meaning.zh: 不戴帽子、赤着脚，形容不拘礼节、生活朴素或隐逸。

examples.zh: 夏夜里老人科头跣足，坐在门口乘凉。
examples.en: On a summer night the old man sat at his door in the cool, bareheaded and barefoot.

examples.zh: 他科头跣足下田干活，一副农夫模样。
examples.en: He worked the fields bareheaded and barefoot, looking like a farmer.

usage.en: Describes casualness or rustic simplicity; 跣 reads xiǎn (barefoot).
usage.zh: 描写随意或乡野朴素；“跣”读 xiǎn，赤脚。

natural: a thirsty horse rushing to a spring

meaning.en: Vigorous, unstoppable momentum, especially in calligraphy or writing.
meaning.zh: 口渴的骏马奔向泉水，形容书法笔势雄健迅猛，也比喻情势急迫、不可阻挡。

examples.zh: 他的草书渴骥奔泉，气势逼人。
examples.en: His cursive script races like a thirsty steed to the spring, full of force.

examples.zh: 球员渴骥奔泉般冲向球门。
examples.en: The player dashed for the goal like a thirsty horse to a spring.

usage.en: Mainly a calligraphy and art-critical image; also lively figurative use. 骥 reads jì (fine horse).
usage.zh: 主要用于书法艺术评论，也可比喻奔赴之势；“骥”读 jì，良马。

natural: harsh and sparing of kindness

meaning.en: Mean-spirited and unkind to others, with little generosity or compassion.
meaning.zh: 待人苛刻无情，很少恩惠。

examples.zh: 那位老板刻薄寡恩，员工纷纷离职。
examples.en: The boss was mean and ungenerous and the staff left one after another.

examples.zh: 史书评价他刻薄寡恩，终致众叛亲离。
examples.en: The histories judge him harsh and unkind, and in the end he was abandoned by all.

usage.en: Pointed criticism of character; used of leaders, bosses, relatives.
usage.zh: 对品格的尖锐批评；多指领导、老板、亲属。

literal: willing · build the hall · willing · raise the frame
natural: willing to lay out the hall, willing to raise the frame

meaning.en: A child who continues and completes his father's work; praise of the heir who carries on the family enterprise.
meaning.zh: 子女能继承并完成父辈的事业。

examples.zh: 他肯堂肯构，把父亲的小店经营成了大公司。
examples.en: He carried on his father's work and turned the little shop into a big company.

examples.zh: 老匠人希望有个肯堂肯构的徒弟。
examples.en: The old craftsman hoped for an apprentice who would carry on his work.

story.en: The 'Great Announcement' uses a metaphor: a father who planned a house, but whose son is unwilling even to lay the foundation, let alone raise the frame.
story.zh: 《尚书·大诰》：“若考作室，既底法，厥子乃弗肯堂，矧肯构？”

date.zh: 西周至战国 · 前11—前3世纪
date.en: Western Zhou to Warring States, 11th–3rd c. BC

usage.en: Praise for a successor, usually within a family; often used in congratulatory messages.
usage.zh: 赞美继承父业的子弟；多用于祝贺语。

natural: the mouth does not match the heart

meaning.en: To say one thing and think another; insincerity.
meaning.zh: 嘴里说的和心里想的不一致。

equivalents: say one thing and mean another

examples.zh: 他嘴上说支持，其实口不应心。
examples.en: He says he supports it, but his words do not match his heart.

examples.zh: 口不应心的客套话，听多了也就腻了。
examples.en: Insincere pleasantries get tiresome when you hear too many.

usage.en: Describes hypocrisy or being forced to speak against one's feelings; close to 口是心非.
usage.zh: 指虚伪或被迫违心说话；近“口是心非”。

natural: the burden of mouth and belly

meaning.en: The trouble of earning a living or of indulging one's appetite; having to compromise for food.
meaning.zh: 为了吃饭或贪图口腹之欲而带来的烦恼和牵累。

examples.zh: 他为口腹之累奔波一生。
examples.en: He ran about all his life to feed himself.

examples.zh: 辞官归田，免去口腹之累。
examples.en: He left office to farm the land, freed from the burden of livelihood.

usage.en: Can mean making a living or gluttony; 累 reads lěi (burden).
usage.zh: 可指谋生之累，也指贪吃之患；“累”读 lěi，牵累。

natural: explain by mouth and sketch with the finger

meaning.en: To explain vividly with both words and gestures, as in teaching.
meaning.zh: 一边口头讲解，一边用手比划，形容教学时认真讲解。

examples.zh: 老师口讲指画，把难题讲得一清二楚。
examples.en: The teacher explained with words and gestures and made the hard problem crystal clear.

examples.zh: 师傅口讲指画，手把手地教徒弟。
examples.en: The master explained and demonstrated, teaching his apprentice hand in hand.

usage.en: Praises patient, hands-on explanation; neutral or mildly positive.
usage.zh: 称赞耐心细致的讲解；中性偏褒。

natural: the blood on the lips is not yet dry

meaning.en: A treaty or oath broken almost as soon as it was sworn.
meaning.zh: 盟誓时涂在嘴上的血还没干，指刚订盟约就违背。

equivalents: break an oath before the ink is dry

examples.zh: 两国口血未干，就撕毁了条约。
examples.en: The blood of the oath was hardly dry before the states tore up the treaty.

examples.zh: 合同口血未干，他就变了卦。
examples.en: Hardly was the contract signed before he went back on it.

usage.en: Used of speedy betrayal of agreements; refers to the ancient oath of smearing blood on the lips.
usage.zh: 形容刚结盟就背约；源自古代歃血盟誓。

natural: the dried-fish shop

meaning.en: Too late to be of use; help that arrives when one is already dead or ruined.
meaning.zh: 等到要救助时，人已像干鱼一样了，比喻求助无望或救援太迟。

examples.zh: 他说得再好听，也不过是枯鱼之肆，救不了急。
examples.en: However fine his words, help that comes too late is no help.

examples.zh: 等批下来，只怕已是枯鱼之肆。
examples.en: By the time approval comes, it may be a case of too little too late.

story.en: Zhuangzi tells of a fish in a dry rut asking for a bucket of water; told to wait for the river to be diverted, it says: 'You may as well look for me in the dried-fish shop!'
story.zh: 《庄子·外物》：“君乃言此，曾不如早索我于枯鱼之肆！”

date.zh: 战国中期 · 前4—前3世纪

usage.en: Rare. Compare 远水不解近渴, which is more common. 肆 reads sì (shop).
usage.zh: 较少见；可参看更常用的“远水不解近渴”；“肆”读 sì，店铺。

natural: leniency and severity complement each other

meaning.en: To govern by combining mercy and strictness, balancing each with the other.
meaning.zh: 治国或管理时，宽厚与严厉相互补充，恰到好处。

examples.zh: 好老师应该宽猛相济，既严格又关怀。
examples.en: A good teacher balances strictness and care.

examples.zh: 治理国家须宽猛相济，不可偏废。
examples.en: Governing a state requires both leniency and severity; neither should be neglected.

story.en: Zichan advised his successor to rule strictly, but Confucius commented that governing should combine leniency and severity: 'leniency tempers severity, and severity tempers leniency, and so government is harmonious.'
story.zh: 《左传·昭公二十年》：“宽以济猛，猛以济宽，政是以和。”

usage.en: A classic principle of governance; applicable to parenting, teaching and management as well.
usage.zh: 经典的治理原则，也适用于育儿、教学和管理。

natural: a piece of jade from Mount Kun

meaning.en: A person of outstanding talent, singled out from the multitude.
meaning.zh: 昆仑山出产的一块玉，比喻才华出众的人。

examples.zh: 这位青年如同昆山片玉，才华卓著。
examples.en: This young man is a jewel among men, outstanding in talent.

examples.zh: 老师称赞她是班里的昆山片玉。
examples.en: The teacher praised her as the gem of the class.

story.en: Asked by Emperor Wu of Jin how he rated himself, Xi Shen replied that he was like 'a branch of cassia from Guilin, a piece of jade from Mount Kun'.
story.zh: 《晋书·郤诜传》：“臣举贤良对策，为天下第一，犹桂林之一枝，昆山之片玉。”

usage.en: Used modestly when someone is chosen or recommended; often paired with 桂林一枝.
usage.zh: 常用于举荐、选拔人才；多与“桂林一枝”并说。

natural: the orchid withers and the jade snaps

meaning.en: The untimely death of a fine person, as an orchid wilts and a jade breaks.
meaning.zh: 兰花枯萎，美玉折断，比喻贤才或美好的人早逝。

equivalents: a bright talent lost too young

examples.zh: 天妒英才，竟致兰摧玉折。
examples.en: Heaven envies the gifted, and the fine talent was lost too soon.

examples.zh: 闻听她兰摧玉折的噩耗，众人皆悲。
examples.en: Hearing of her untimely death, everyone grieved.

usage.en: Used in obituaries and elegies for the young or the gifted; formal, mournful.
usage.zh: 用于悼念年轻或有才者；庄重悲痛。

natural: orchid at the start, willow-fluff at the end

meaning.en: A marriage that begins beautifully but ends in separation; a good start, a sad ending.
meaning.zh: 开头如兰花般美好，结果却像柳絮般飘散，多指婚姻始合终离。

equivalents: a lovely start with a sad ending

examples.zh: 他们的婚姻是兰因絮果，令人唏嘘。
examples.en: Their marriage began so well and ended so sadly.

examples.zh: 别让一段好缘分成了兰因絮果。
examples.en: Don't let a good match end in separation.

usage.en: Mostly used of broken marriages or relationships; literary and rather sentimental.
usage.zh: 多指婚姻或感情始合终离；书面语，带感伤。
